US Proposes Stricter J 1 Visa Rules That Could Affect Indian Researchers, Doctors And Professors
articles.description: The US State Department has proposed significant reforms to the J 1 Exchange Visitor Program, impacting numerous Indian professionals, including researchers and educators. New regulations include stricter compliance measures, grounds for terminating J 1 status, and tighter deadlines for program extensions. Participants may face fixed admission periods and must apply for extensions well in advance. Additionally, record management within the Student and Exchange Visitor Information System (SEVIS) will be streamlined. The proposed changes aim to enhance program integrity and oversight, with a public comment period of 60 days.

articles.title: Psychology says people who never apologize even if they are at fault aren't necessarily rude or careless: What this behavior reveals?
articles.description: Psychology says people who are never apologize even if they are at fault aren't always simply rude or careless. Their behaviour can be linked to defensiveness, fear of blame, self-image, difficulty accepting responsibility, or a different view of what happened. Research on apologies shows that admitting wrongdoing can affect relationships, responsibility, trust and conflict. Understanding these reasons can help explain why some people avoid saying sorry.
